title: Two Sum
description:
Given an array of integers `nums` and an integer `target`, return indices of the two numbers such that they add up to `target`.

You may assume that each input would have exactly one solution, and you may not use the same element twice.
editorial:
## One-Pass Hash Map
Store each value's index as you scan left to right. Before inserting `nums[i]`, check whether its complement `target - nums[i]` is already in the map. Time `O(n)`, space `O(n)`.
hints: Store previously seen values in a hash map mapping value -> index.

title: Contains Duplicate
description: Given an integer array `nums`, return `True` if any value appears at least twice in the array, and return `False` if every element is distinct.

solutions.python:
def contains_duplicate(nums):
    return len(set(nums)) < len(nums)

editorial:
## Hash Set Deduplication
Insert elements into a set; if an element is already present (or `len(set(nums)) < len(nums)`), a duplicate exists. Time `O(n)`, space `O(n)`.
hints: Compare the length of the array against the size of a set constructed from it.

title: Valid Anagram
description: Given two strings `s` and `t`, return `True` if `t` is an anagram of `s`, and `False` otherwise.
editorial:
## Frequency Counting
Two strings are anagrams iff they have identical character frequency distributions. Runs in `O(n)` time and `O(1)` alphabet space.
hints: Count character frequencies in both strings and compare.

title: Group Anagrams
description: Given an array of strings `strs`, group the anagrams together. Return a list of groups where each group is sorted alphabetically and groups are ordered by their first element.
editorial:
## Canonical Signature Key
Every anagram family shares the same sorted character signature (or 26-element count tuple). Map each signature to its bucket in `O(N * K log K)` (or `O(N * K)` with counts).
hints: Use the sorted characters of each word as a hash map key.

title: Top K Frequent Elements
description: Given an integer array `nums` and an integer `k`, return the `k` most frequent elements sorted in ascending order.
editorial:
## Bucket Sort by Frequency
Frequencies lie in `[1, n]`. Indexing buckets by frequency lets you collect the top `k` elements in `O(n)` linear time without sorting all keys.
hints: Count frequencies, then place each value into bucket[freq].

title: Product of Array Except Self
description: Given an integer array `nums`, return an array `answer` such that `answer[i]` is equal to the product of all elements of `nums` except `nums[i]`, in `O(n)` time without using division.

solutions.python:
def product_except_self(nums):
    n = len(nums)
    res = [1] * n
    prefix = 1
    for i in range(n):
        res[i] = prefix
        prefix *= nums[i]
    suffix = 1
    for i in range(n - 1, -1, -1):
        res[i] *= suffix
        suffix *= nums[i]
    return res

editorial:
## Prefix × Suffix Decomposition
`answer[i] = (product of elements left of i) * (product of elements right of i)`. Two linear sweeps compute this in `O(n)` time and `O(1)` extra space beyond the output array.
hints: Store prefix products in res on a left-to-right pass, then multiply by running suffix products right-to-left.

title: Longest Consecutive Sequence
description: Given an unsorted array of integers `nums`, return the length of the longest consecutive elements sequence in `O(n)` time.
editorial:
## Sequence Start Detection
Only start counting upward from `x` when `x - 1` is NOT in the set. Each integer is visited at most twice overall, guaranteeing `O(n)` total time.
hints: Only expand forward from numbers x where x - 1 is absent from the set.

title: Valid Palindrome
description: Given a string `s`, return `True` if it is a palindrome after converting all uppercase letters into lowercase and removing all non-alphanumeric characters.

examples.input: s = 'A man, a plan, a canal: Panama'

constraints: O(n) time, O(1) space with two pointers

solutions.python:
def is_palindrome(s):
    l, r = 0, len(s) - 1
    while l < r:
        while l < r and not s[l].isalnum(): l += 1
        while l < r and not s[r].isalnum(): r -= 1
        if s[l].lower() != s[r].lower(): return False
        l += 1; r -= 1
    return True

editorial:
## Converging Pointers
Move `l` rightward and `r` leftward skipping non-alphanumeric characters, verifying lowercase equality at each pair in `O(n)` time and `O(1)` auxiliary space.

input.s: A man, a plan, a canal: Panama

hints: Advance left and right pointers inward, skipping non-alphanumeric characters.

title: 3Sum
description: Given an integer array `nums`, return all unique triplets `[nums[i], nums[j], nums[k]]` such that `i != j != k` and `nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k] == 0`, with each triplet and the outer list sorted ascending.
editorial:
## Sort + Two-Pointer Sweep
Sort `nums` first (`O(n log n)`). Fix `nums[i]` (skipping duplicates) and run a converging two-pointer search on `nums[i+1:]` for `-nums[i]`. Total time `O(n^2)`.
hints: Sort the array first, fix one element, and run two pointers on the suffix.

title: Container With Most Water
description: Given `height`, an array of non-negative vertical line heights, find two lines that together with the x-axis form a container holding the maximum amount of water.

solutions.python:
def max_area(height):
    l, r = 0, len(height) - 1
    best = 0
    while l < r:
        best = max(best, (r - l) * min(height[l], height[r]))
        if height[l] < height[r]: l += 1
        else: r -= 1
    return best

editorial:
## Greedy Pointer Elimination
Area is limited by the shorter wall. Moving the taller wall inward can never increase area (width shrinks and height cannot exceed the shorter wall), so always advance the shorter pointer.
hints: Start pointers at both ends and move the shorter wall inward.

title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
description: Given an array `prices` where `prices[i]` is the price of a stock on day `i`, return the maximum profit achievable from one buy followed by one sell. Return `0` if no profit is possible.
editorial:
## Running Minimum Window
Track the lowest buy price seen so far (`min_price`) and update `best = max(best, price - min_price)` in a single `O(n)` pass.
hints: Track the minimum price seen so far as you iterate.

title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
description: Given a string `s`, find the length of the longest substring without repeating characters.
editorial:
## Dynamic Sliding Window
Maintain `[l, r]` with all distinct characters. Map each character to its latest index; whenever `s[r]` collides inside `[l, r]`, jump `l = last[s[r]] + 1` in `O(1)`.
hints: Store each character's last seen index to advance the left boundary directly.

title: Longest Repeating Character Replacement
description: Given an uppercase string `s` and integer `k`, you may replace at most `k` characters with any other uppercase letter. Return the length of the longest substring containing the same letter.
editorial:
## Window Validity Invariant
A window of length `W` is valid iff `W - max_freq <= k`. Keeping the historical maximum `maxf` lets the window expand whenever a larger valid span is found in `O(n)` time.
hints: A window is valid when window_length - max_char_frequency <= k.

title: Valid Parentheses
description: Given a string `s` containing only `'('`, `')'`, `'{'`, `'}'`, `'['`, and `']'`, determine if the input string has properly matched and nested brackets.
editorial:
## LIFO Bracket Matching
Push opening brackets onto a stack; each closing bracket must match the top of the stack. Valid iff no mismatch occurs and the stack finishes empty.
hints: Map each closing bracket to its matching opener and verify against stack.pop().

title: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array
description: Given a sorted rotated array `nums` of unique elements, return the minimum element in `O(log n)` time.

solutions.python:
def find_min(nums):
    l, r = 0, len(nums) - 1
    while l < r:
        mid = (l + r) // 2
        if nums[mid] > nums[r]: l = mid + 1
        else: r = mid
    return nums[l]

editorial:
## Pivot Comparison Against Right Endpoint
If `nums[mid] > nums[r]`, the rotation pivot (minimum) must lie strictly to the right (`l = mid + 1`); otherwise it lies at or left of `mid` (`r = mid`).
hints: Compare nums[mid] with nums[r] to decide which half holds the inflection point.

title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
description: Given a rotated sorted array `nums` of distinct integers and `target`, return the index of `target` if it is in `nums`, or `-1` otherwise, in `O(log n)` time.
editorial:
## Half-Sorted Invariant
At every midpoint, at least one of `[l, mid]` or `[mid, r]` is strictly sorted. Check whether `target` falls within the sorted half's bounds to discard half the array each step.
hints: Determine which half is sorted via nums[l] <= nums[mid], then test if target lies inside it.

title: Reverse Linked List
description: Given a singly linked list represented as an array of node values `values`, build the linked list, reverse its pointers iteratively in `O(n)` time and `O(1)` space, and return the reversed values as a list.
editorial:
## Three-Pointer Iterative Reversal
Track `(prev, cur, nxt)`. At each step save `nxt = cur.next`, rewire `cur.next = prev`, and slide `(prev, cur) = (cur, nxt)`.
hints: Save cur.next before flipping cur.next = prev.

title: Merge Two Sorted Lists
description: Merge two sorted integer lists `list1` and `list2` into one sorted list in `O(n + m)` time.

solutions.python:
def merge_two_lists(list1, list2):
    i = j = 0
    out = []
    while i < len(list1) and j < len(list2):
        if list1[i] <= list2[j]: out.append(list1[i]); i += 1
        else: out.append(list2[j]); j += 1
    out.extend(list1[i:]); out.extend(list2[j:])
    return out

editorial:
## Dummy Head / Two-Pointer Merge
Advance whichever pointer has the smaller head value, then attach the remaining non-empty tail in `O(n + m)` time.
hints: Use two indices i and j and append the smaller element each step.

title: Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
description: Given a binary tree encoded in level-order array representation (`null` for missing nodes), return its maximum depth (number of nodes along the longest root-to-leaf path).
editorial:
## Recursive Tree Height
`depth(node) = 0` if `node is None`, else `1 + max(depth(left), depth(right))`. Runs in `O(n)` time and `O(h)` stack space.
hints: For level-order index i, children sit at 2*i + 1 and 2*i + 2.

title: Validate Binary Search Tree
description: Given a binary tree in level-order array form (`null` for missing nodes), return `True` if it is a strictly valid Binary Search Tree.
constraints: All left descendants < node < all right descendants
editorial:
## Narrowing Interval Invariant
Checking only immediate children misses violations deeper in a subtree. Pass `(lo, hi)` bounds down each branch: left inherits `(lo, node.val)`, right inherits `(node.val, hi)`.
hints: Propagate open bounds (lo, hi) down the recursion.

title: Implement Trie (Prefix Tree)
description: Process a sequence of Trie operations `ops` (`['insert', word]`, `['search', word]`, `['startsWith', prefix]`) and return the list of boolean results produced by `search` and `startsWith` calls.
editorial:
## Prefix Sharing
Each Trie node maps characters to child nodes plus a terminal flag `#`. Both `insert` and `search`/`startsWith` run in `O(L)` time where `L` is the word length.
hints: Store child maps and a boolean end-of-word marker at each node.

title: Find Median from Data Stream
description: Given a stream of integers `nums`, return a list where the `i`-th entry is the median of `nums[0..i]` (as a float).
constraints: O(n log n) total using two heaps
editorial:
## Balanced Two-Heap Partition
Keep the smaller half in a max-heap `lo` and the larger half in a min-heap `hi` with `0 <= len(lo) - len(hi) <= 1`. Each insertion takes `O(log n)` and median lookup is `O(1)`.
hints: Maintain a max-heap for the lower half and a min-heap for the upper half.

title: Combination Sum
description: Given an array of distinct integers `candidates` and a `target`, return all unique combinations of `candidates` where the chosen numbers sum to `target` (same number may be chosen unlimited times).
editorial:
## Non-Decreasing Decision Tree
Passing `start = i` (allowing reuse of `candidates[i]` while forbidding earlier indices) generates every unique multiset combination without duplicates.
hints: Sort candidates so you can prune as soon as candidates[i] > remaining.

title: Number of Islands
description: Given an `m x n` 2D grid of `'1'`s (land) and `'0'`s (water), return the number of connected islands (4-directionally adjacent `'1'`s).
editorial:
## Flood-Fill Connected Components
Whenever an unvisited `'1'` cell is encountered, increment the island counter and flood-fill its entire 4-connected component via DFS/BFS.
hints: Flood-fill each newly discovered '1' cell and mark its connected component visited.

title: Course Schedule
description: There are `num_courses` courses labeled `0..num_courses-1` and prerequisite pairs `[course, prereq]`. Return `True` if you can finish all courses (i.e., the prerequisite graph has no cycle).
editorial:
## Kahn's Topological Sort
Repeatedly dequeue nodes with in-degree `0` and decrement neighbors' in-degrees. All courses can be finished iff every node is processed (`taken == num_courses`).
hints: Use Kahn's BFS topological sort with an in-degree array.

title: Alien Dictionary
description: Given a sorted list of words in an alien language, derive a valid character ordering (breaking ties lexicographically) or return `''` if the ordering is invalid.
constraints: Return '' if a cycle or invalid prefix ordering exists
editorial:
## Precedence Graph Extraction
Compare each adjacent word pair at their first differing index to add directed edge `a -> b`. Guard against invalid prefix ordering (`len(w1) > len(w2)` and `w1.startswith(w2)`), then run topological sort.
hints: Only the FIRST differing character between adjacent words yields a precedence edge.

title: Climbing Stairs
description: You are climbing a staircase of `n` steps. Each time you can climb `1` or `2` steps. Return the number of distinct ways to reach the top.
editorial:
## Recurrence `dp[i] = dp[i-1] + dp[i-2]`
Every path to step `i` arrives from either `i - 1` or `i - 2`, reducing to `O(n)` time and `O(1)` space.
hints: dp[i] = dp[i - 1] + dp[i - 2] with only the previous two values needed.

title: House Robber
description: Given an integer array `nums` representing cash in each house along a street, return the maximum amount you can rob without robbing two adjacent houses.
editorial:
## Take-or-Skip Transition
At house `i`, either skip it (`prev1`) or rob it plus best up to `i - 2` (`prev2 + nums[i]`). Runs in `O(n)` time and `O(1)` space.
hints: Maintain only the best totals for i - 1 and i - 2.

title: Coin Change
description: Given coin denominations `coins` and a total `amount`, return the fewest number of coins needed to make up `amount`, or `-1` if impossible.
editorial:
## Bottom-Up Unbounded DP
`dp[a] = min(1 + dp[a - c] for c in coins if c <= a)`, with `dp[0] = 0`. Runs in `O(amount * len(coins))`.
hints: Initialize dp[0] = 0 and dp[1..amount] = Infinity.

title: Unique Paths
description: A robot starts at the top-left of an `m x n` grid and can only move right or down. Return the number of unique paths to the bottom-right corner.
editorial:
## Space-Compressed Grid DP
`dp[r][c] = dp[r-1][c] + dp[r][c-1]` collapses to a single `O(n)` row updated left-to-right.
hints: Each cell's path count equals top + left.

title: Longest Common Subsequence
description: Given two strings `text1` and `text2`, return the length of their longest common subsequence.
editorial:
## Suffix Alignment Table
Match characters diagonally (`1 + dp[i+1][j+1]`) or skip one character from either string (`max(dp[i+1][j], dp[i][j+1])`).
hints: If text1[i] == text2[j], take 1 + dp[i+1][j+1]; else take max of skipping either char.

title: Maximum Subarray (Kadane's Algorithm)
description: Given an integer array `nums`, find the contiguous subarray with the largest sum and return its sum.
editorial:
## Kadane's Prefix Reset
A negative running sum can only hurt any future extension, so reset `cur = max(x, cur + x)` at every step in `O(n)` time and `O(1)` space.
hints: Discard the running subarray whenever it becomes worse than starting fresh at nums[i].

title: Jump Game
description: Given an array `nums` where `nums[i]` is your maximum jump length from index `i`, return `True` if you can reach the last index starting from index `0`.
editorial:
## Farthest Reach Invariant
Maintain the maximum reachable index `reach`. If index `i > reach`, we are stranded; otherwise update `reach = max(reach, i + nums[i])`.
hints: Track the farthest index reachable so far; fail if i > reach.

title: Merge Intervals
description: Given an array of `[start, end]` intervals, merge all overlapping intervals and return an array of non-overlapping intervals covering all input ranges.
editorial:
## Sort by Start & Sweep
After sorting by start coordinate, any overlapping interval is guaranteed to collide with the last interval in `merged`.
hints: Sort intervals by start time, then extend the last merged interval whenever start <= prev_end.

title: Spiral Matrix
description: Given an `m x n` `matrix`, return all elements of the matrix in clockwise spiral order.
editorial:
## Shrinking Four-Wall Boundaries
Maintain `(top, bottom, left, right)`. After sweeping each edge, shrink its wall inward and guard the bottom/left sweeps against crossing bounds.
hints: Track four walls (top, bottom, left, right) and shrink each after traversing it.

title: Missing Number
description: Given an array `nums` containing `n` distinct numbers in the range `[0, n]`, return the single number in the range that is missing from the array in `O(n)` time and `O(1)` space.
editorial:
## XOR Self-Cancellation
Since `a ^ a = 0` and `a ^ 0 = a`, XORing all indices `0..n` with all elements of `nums` cancels every present number, leaving only the missing value.
hints: XOR every index 0..n with every element in nums, or subtract sum(nums) from n*(n+1)//2.

title: Counting Bits
description: Given an integer `n`, return an array `ans` of length `n + 1` where `ans[i]` is the number of `1`s in the binary representation of `i`, in `O(n)` time.
editorial:
## Bitwise DP Recurrence
Shifting `i` right drops the LSB (`i & 1`), giving `dp[i] = dp[i >> 1] + (i & 1)` in `O(1)` per integer.
hints: Relate popcount(i) to popcount(i >> 1) plus the least significant bit (i & 1).
